population_note_text: Not walked from the books population: every row is one (section, payee) tax amount already identified as a shortfall by 'TDS on payments made' or 'Partners (s.40(b), s.194T)', with whatever deduction/payment dates the books or documents establish. An unsupplied date is never guessed; it drives a range instead.

figures.definition_text: Reference date for every maximum bound: the return due date from rules[due_dates], or the report date, as supplied by the caller -- this test never reads rules[due_dates] itself.
Rows whose payee's foreseeability is not classified in the client's list of payees: priced from each credit's own date and flagged on their finding.
s.206C(7) rate, per month or part of a month (s.206C(7), status=partial).
s.201(1A) post-deduction rate, per month or part of a month (s.201(1A), status=VP).
s.201(1A) pre-deduction rate, per month or part of a month (s.201(1A), status=VP).
Rows (deducted_date unknown, s.201(1A)) where a payee return-filing date was supplied for the Form 26A relief scenario.
Rows (deducted_date unknown, s.201(1A)) where no payee return-filing date was supplied -- the Form 26A relief scenario could not be computed.

Sum of interest_26a_relief_<row> in the higher-rate scenario: every row at a payee's higher rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well, over only the rows where a payee filing date was supplied -- a partial sum over a subset, never compared directly to the range.

Sum of interest_26a_relief_<row> in the lower-rate scenario: every row at a payee's lower rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well, over only the rows where a payee filing date was supplied -- a partial sum over a subset, never compared directly to the range.

Sum of each row's maximum with every credit's tax from its own date (interest_max_own_date_<row>, or interest_max_<row> where a row has no such figure) in the higher-rate scenario: every row at a payee's higher rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well.

Sum of each row's maximum with every credit's tax from its own date (interest_max_own_date_<row>, or interest_max_<row> where a row has no such figure) in the lower-rate scenario: every row at a payee's lower rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well.
The ceiling of the combined range: the higher-rate scenario's maximum, each credit's tax running from its own date (one reading of s.194C(5) and its proviso, pending the CA's confirmation).
Sum of interest_min_<row> in the higher-rate scenario: every row at a payee's higher rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well.
Sum of interest_min_<row> in the lower-rate scenario: every row at a payee's lower rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well.
The floor of the combined range: the lower-rate scenario's minimum.
Sum of tax_<row> in the higher-rate scenario: every row at a payee's higher rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well.
Sum of tax_<row> in the lower-rate scenario: every row at a payee's lower rate, and every row at a single rate -- never a payee's row at the other rate as well.
